## v5.1.0 — mentions, thread unreads, and labels on every message

![After the weekend I had, and now the printer is acting up. One search, and the PIN that had been waiting in #facilities for five months.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jtalk22/slack-mcp-server/v5.1.0/docs/images/hero-v2.gif)

Put your agent inside your Slack. Zero bots, zero admin queues, no Business+ upgrade — 20+ tools for stealth search, thread parsing and mention tracking. Every message attributed. No stored token on our side.

```sh
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --setup
```

### Measured on a real workspace

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Conversations the catch-up reported while ten mentions waited | 0 | 7 |
| Mentions it could see | 0 | 10 |
| Colleagues labelled `unknown` on a 20-message channel | 11 | 0 |
| Write tools registered under `--read-only` | 4 | 0 |
| Credential lifetime claimed | "1–2 weeks" | measured: 94 days and counting |

### The catch-up now sees every mention and thread reply

`slack_conversations_unreads` filtered on `unread_count_display` from `conversations.list`, which is zero the moment a channel has been opened. It now also reads `client.counts`, the endpoint Slack's own web client uses for its sidebar badges, and merges the two: per-conversation mention counts, unread thread replies, and the conversations a single listing page never reaches. Mentions sort above unread volume.

`client.counts` is undocumented, so every read of it is guarded and the response names which endpoint answered. When it fails, the tool degrades to exactly the previous view and says what is missing.

### Every message says who wrote it

Slack is a shared bus — Slack Connect participants, guests, apps relaying content from outside Slack — and the same toolset that reads also writes. Every message now carries `origin` (`self`, `internal`, `external`, `bot`, `unknown`) and `author_trusted`, from fields Slack already returns, at no extra API call.

Building it found something worse: Slack omits `team` from messages written inside your own workspace, so a naive classifier calls half your colleagues unknown. A conversation Slack reports as not shared cannot hold an outside author, so a team-less author there is internal.

### Also new

- **`--read-only` / `SLACK_MCP_READ_ONLY=1`** — the write tools are withheld from `tools/list` *and* refused at dispatch. An absent tool needs no trust.
- **`--doctor --security`** — six checks of your own setup, each with the command that tightens it. No score.
- **`slack_session_report`** — messages read, how many were outside-authored and by which origin, writes attempted, writes held. Counts only; never message text.
- **`continuity` on `slack_catch_me_up`** — commitments, owner gaps, open questions, each row with the text that matched and a permalink. The rules are shallow and the output says so.
- **`externally_shared` on `slack_list_conversations`** — from fields already returned, no extra call.
- **A published prompt-injection corpus** ([docs/INJECTION-CORPUS.md](https://github.com/jtalk22/slack-mcp-server/blob/main/docs/INJECTION-CORPUS.md)) — bidi overrides, zero-width splits, tool-call mimicry, bot relays, attacker-settable identity fields, so other MCP authors can test their own servers.
- **CodeQL and OSV-Scanner** on every change, and signed npm provenance on every release.

### Fixed

- The strict send hold could be switched off by the call it was meant to restrain, and `slack_catch_me_up` never armed it at all.
- The setup wizard described an extraction path the code does not run, and repeated one fixed instruction whatever the failure. It now follows the reason code and prints the client configuration instead of linking to a page about it.
- Commands an `npx` user cannot run were removed from the docs and the bug-report template.
- Identity-keyed caches are cleared on a token refresh; a refresh can land on a different workspace.
- `slack_catch_me_up` and `slack_conversations_history` classified the same message differently; both now resolve the conversation's sharing state.

### The limits, stated

A provenance label is advice to the calling model: unsigned, strippable downstream. The `strict` hold is released by a flag the caller sets, so it records a send without proving a human approved it. Display names and channel topics still reach the model unlabelled. `--read-only` is the only guarantee that does not depend on the model. All of it is in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/jtalk22/slack-mcp-server/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

### Compatibility

Default behaviour adds keys and removes none. `SLACK_MCP_PROVENANCE=off` restores the previous output shape. The `provenance` argument on a read may tighten labelling and no longer loosen it. Node 20 and up.

### Install

```sh
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --setup
claude mcp add slack -- npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp
```

```sh
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --doctor --security   # check your own setup
npx -y @jtalk22/slack-mcp --read-only           # read Slack, never write to it
```
